My husband & I have 2 teenagers. So between the 4 of us, we have 4 Android phones, 4 tablets, & 4 laptops. We go through a lot of micro USB cables. Over the years, I have learned that not all USB cables are created equally! First of all, the plastic the covers the ends of the cables is a solid material. We have had several cables that with use, bend or break in the place where the actual cable meets. Since this is all one piece on the ends, that's not going to happen. The cable is a good length. It's long enough that if it's plugged in a lower outlet, it can still reach the end table, but it's not too long that you have a lot of excess cable getting in the way. I love that it's available in a few different colors. I selected the lime green one so it's very easy to see which cable is mine! And if anyone walks away with it, I know which child has it! At first I had this in my car with a car charger. But over the last week, I never was in my car for more than 10 minutes at a time, so I couldn't get an accurate feel for whether or not it was a fast syncing cable. This morning I brought it inside and plugged into one of our charging stations. My phone was at 50% so I was curious to learn how quickly it would charge using this cable. Within 10 minutes my phone had charged an additional 10%. When I checked thirty minutes later, it was fully charged. I was quite pleased with that. I have a Nexus 5 phone and depending on where I am charging it, it often takes longer than that.

*I received the Haweel Micro USB cable for the purpose of trying it out & reviewing it. My thoughts & opinions are my own.

This hits the mark when it comes to potency, with each capsule providing 50 billion CFUs. However, there's conflicting information with regard to the strains represented. On the bottle four "proprietary" strain groupings are listed; in the product listing it states there are 9 different strains consisting of Lactobacilli and Bifidobacteria varieties. I don't know which is correct, and I don't care for product bottle information to be vague about what's in the capsule.

The other issue that is uncertain is whether this contains a prebiotic. In the product listing it states it includes FOS (a common prebiotic) but does not list the amount. On the bottle there's no mention at all of any prebiotic.

Given the wide variety of probiotics on the market where the manufacturer is far more transparent as to what specifically is in the formulation, I don't consider this brand to be a good option. Since the potency level is very good, and it is a US-made product, I'll give it 2 stars, but limited and/or contradictory information in a health care product is not the hallmark of a good brand.

I was a Chef back in the day. I owned my own set of Henckel knives custom sharpened and the handles wrapped with wax and jute. Also, I owned my own set of pans, again custom wrapped in jute... I even owned my own grill spatulas sharpened on one edge and yes wrapped in jute and wax. I know what tools it takes..as any pro would...to do a job. SHARP KNIVES are by far the No. 1 tool for the cook... whether they be a sous chef, a pantry chef or "line" cook. Most chefs have their knives PROFESSIONALLY SHARPENED!!! We may use a "steel' to hone our knives during work but we depend on Pro Sharpening services to take care of my $1000.00 Henckels.

I'm not a Chef anymore. But I still like to cook for friends and family and own some pretty nice, high quality cutlery. I have tried 3 different "do-it-yourself" knife sharpening tools that work on the "just pull and draw on the v shaped slot and voila, your knife is sharpened."

They do not and will not EVER SHARPEN YOUR KNIVES!!!! After using this "sharpener" it basically turned my nice Cuisinart Chefs knife into a butter knife. I tried it out on several other Cuisinart knives and again pretty much turned all of them into butter knifes.

I returned this and bought a good 1000/6000 grit whetstone and was able to "recover" my kitchen knives and as a bonus, able to sharpen by 440c pocket knives.

Summary: these quick sharpen pull and draw knife sharpeners will not work! Either get your cutlery PROFESSIONALLY SHARPENED or get a good whetstone set and learn how to sharpen yourself.

I have four of these now. They work really well, and consistently. As long as they are plugged into a power outlet, the clock continues to run, and the thing plugged into it goes on/off at the times you set. When I'm away, I use them on my lights. When I'm home, I use them on kitchen appliances to ensure that they are off during times I don't use them. You can also just set them to 'on' when you're home, or store them for the next time you need them.

It's a little counter-intuitive the first time you set it up, but, once you get the hang of it, it's very easy.

Unlike digital timers, you don't have to worry about small power outages. The only problem I can foresee is if there is a long outage, then the clock will be wrong and it will be going on/off at different times. However, compared to not working at all at the slightest outage, I feel that this is a very minor drawback.

I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

If you are new to home security camera systems, I recommend going with wired (non-WiFi), NVR or computer based recorders run with systems such as Blue Iris. This type of system is infinitely more secure and stable. While initial setup costs are a bit more the security it affords is worth every penny. It always pays to research the products, discuss them with those in the field, understand vulnerabilities and PLAN YOUR SYSTEM PRIOR TO PURCHASING ANYTHING. If you are at all tech savvy at all you can do it. While there is a bit of a learning curve it is not awful and in the end you will be thankful for the time you spent in the beginning as it will save you time, money and endless frustration.

I have set up, tested and reviewed more security systems and individual products than I can possibly remember. Without question my go to solution for home security solutions is a computer based, Blue Iris system with POE cameras run off of quality POE switches. This type of system is not only easy to operate but is highly secure.

As with any component there are a host of factors to consider. In terms of cameras more megapixels is not always better. For instance 2MP cameras often perform better in low light while 5MP will allow for more detail when lighting is good. One disadvantage of higher megapixel cameras is the recordings will take up more hard drive space. Depending on the number of cameras, this can become a larger concern.

When I saw this camera at this price point I knew it was something I needed to check out. I appreciated the fact it was 2MP because with this lens you are not going to want to be eating up the hard drive space required for a 5MP.

I was able to get it set up within my Blue Iris system after playing with it for a while. Typically this takes me no more than a couple of minutes - this camera required much more extensive programming in order to have it functional.

Once I did have it up and working image quality is substandard even compared to other cameras with similar specs.

I figured it still could be utilized as a tertiary filler camera but it kept going offline for absolutely no reason. When a camera is connected via PoE to Blue Iris this simply should not be an issue unless there are issues with the camera itself.

While the price point is excellent on this camera, unfortunately this is an example of getting what you pay for. In my four months of testing this camera has proven to be unreliable, difficult to connect and keep connected and the images captured are far lower quality than expected from cameras with similar specs.

Vinegar has been used as a remedy since the days of Hippocrates. The ancient Greek doctor treated wounds with it. In recent years, people have explored apple cider vinegar as a way to lose weight, improve heart health, and even treat dandruff.

Many of these claims aren’t supported by modern research. But some studies have found that acetic acid -- which gives vinegar its distinctive taste and smell -- may help with a variety of conditions:

Japanese scientists found that drinking vinegar might help reduce obesity.

One small study found that vinegar improved blood sugar and insulin levels in a group of people with type 2 diabetes.
Vinegar also has chemicals known as polyphenols. They’re antioxidants that can curb cell damage that can lead to other diseases, such as cancer. But studies on whether vinegar actually lowers your chances of having cancer are mixed.

The Downsides...
Drinking a lot of apple cider vinegar can damage your teeth, hurt your throat, and upset your stomach. Also:

Though some studies have been promising, there’s still little evidence that drinking apple cider vinegar helps you lose weight.
It may also cause your potassium levels to drop too low. Your muscles and nerves need that nutrient to work the way they should.

Another study of people with type 1 diabetes found that apple cider vinegar slows the rate food and liquids leave the stomach to be digested. That makes it harder to control your blood sugar level.

It might also affect medications that treat diabetes and heart disease, as well as diuretics (medicines that help your body get rid of water and salt) and laxatives.

In short, apple cider vinegar probably won’t hurt you. Enjoy it in your diet because it’s calorie-free, adds lots of flavor to food, and has health benefits. But it’s not a miracle cure.

This is a powerful full-size massage gun with 30 intensity levels. It comes with a user pamphlet, the gun, A/C charging cable, eight massage tools, and a case.

The user pamphlet is lacking in description or use of all the tools. They need to provide a picture with a label of what each one is. Based on previous experience with other massage tools, below is what I believe these tools are and can be used for.

- ball head - for shoulder and neck

- post-like head (looks like a graduated ball head) - for use on softer parts of body such as inside thigh

- paddle head - suitable for spine

- U-shaped head - for both sides of spine, triceps, hips, and legs

- flat head with nubs - for massaging all muscle parts in the entire body for relaxation

- finger-like head (i.e. conical head) - for concentrated uses such on specific pain points

- knobbed head (i.e. one with four prongs) - suitable for calf muscles

- T-shaped curved head (i.e. long curved head with nubs) - good for arms and legs as it curves around those areas.

I first charged this gun for about four hours until the blue light on bottom was on fully. To use this I just inserted the head that I wanted, flipped the switch on the bottom of the handle to the ON position, and then pressed the ON button on the gun and + button on the LED dial to the intensity level I wanted (from 1 to 30). The ON/OFF button on the LED can be pressed to suspend operation and the - to reduce intensity. Once the unit turns on, the battery level is displayed on the bottom of the handle. The latest intensity is remembered from the previous session

I do not use any massage gun for more than a few minutes. When I am totally done, I just slide the switch on the bottom of the handle to the OFF position. There are no other features of this gun. It is simple, simple, simple and has worked every time. However, this gun is not useful for me unless I have someone else helping me or the issue is in an area I can reach, such as my thighs or calves. Nevertheless, I did not mark this down for that reason as that is no fault of the gun. These type items really require an assistant.

In summary, this works best if someone else is applying the pressure with the gun to my muscles--such as the back. For someone who is used to this type of gun or has an assistant, a massage gun like this can be great. The ease of use of this gun is its best feature because it is no frills--just turn on and go. I also love the green color. The one negative is that the user pamphlet does not list a picture of the tools with what they are used for. There are some instructions for shoulder, neck, and knee issues but they only use the T-shaped head or U-shaped head.  The current price of $99.99 ($139.99 minus $40) is excellent for this gun. This receives 4.5 stars from me as a massage gun.

(WARNING- This is an in depth review for those who are truly looking for information to help in buying decisions. If you prefer the shortened version, see the section labeled THE BOTTOM LINE)

I have a blender which is about 16 years old now- a Juicelady Blender which was not anything particularly high end at the time of purchase. It is glass with a simple base and the base has a bunch of speeds with ice crushing, and simple blades. The top fits decently and we have used it a lot in these years. Recently someone was kind enough to get me this Oster Reverse Crush Counterforms Blender because our bedraggled blender has the buttons worn off and is quite old. It was such an amazing thing to receive. I could not wait to try this out. Surely it would be a step up..

WHAT IS THIS BLENDER LIKE?
A bit wider than most other glass blenders I have used, this one promised to be an interesting experience. The base was sleek and really nice looking. I loved the idea of the different programs to run on it. The blades are curved in an upward position and look very ready to blend the heck out of anything you throw at it.

The ring that seals the bottom was okay, not anything marvelous, but okay. The base screwed on very nicely. The top, however was cheesy and cheap. I did not like it at all. It did not fit on tight and was harder than it should be. No rubbery feel at all to it. There is a domed cap that fits into the lid, but taking it off is an experience. You need to turn off the blender to remove the dome if you want to add anything.

WHAT I NEED A BLENDER FOR
We have a very active household when it comes to blenders. Due to previous issues with children breaking appliances, we have a Vitamix for heavy duty jobs which I am the only one who uses it, and then we have the household blender which the rest of the house uses constantly. Here is a list of what we use the household blender for:
sauces
smoothies
sesame milk
cold soups
other nut milks

There are other uses I can not recall at the moment, but that is the basic idea. Another thing that I would like to have the blender do is a decent green smoothie. That is easier said than done. My husband has to have them now and I prefer him to have his own appliance so I can have the pleasure of using one thing that is not used to death by the rest of the family before I can actually use it myself. It is a happier household that way since I am a raw foodie with a paleo twist so I need the Vitamix constantly. I would prefer to use it for that.

HOW DOES THIS BLENDER WORK?
My husband has come up with some pretty good methods for making the best out of our appliances. He tends to see their strengths and really get them to work well for certain processes. When we got this blender, he immediately proceeded to clean and wash it for its first use. After studying it intensely for a few moments, he then put the blender to the first test- sesame milk. He started with it on medium and began to shout from the kitchen that he was afraid it might die. He moved it up to high and it was okay but left the milk pretty chunky.

Then he took out the very old blender and did the same thing and it was smooth. He also tried a few other more watery things and was very upset about the low and medium speeds as they seemed they would die. The reverse was so pathetic that he could not believe they made it that way.

MY TEST
I decided I would try it myself and see if I could get it to perform better.

I performed a test of the most important thing in our household- green smoothie. I started with a half a frozen banana and a tiny handful of frozen black currants. I filled the blender halfway with water. I put it on frozen drink mode. It did an okay job going back and forth, perhaps my husband didn't get it right yesterday..

Then I tasted it so far. ICK. So chunky it was ridiculous. It was not a pleasure to drink.

I then got some fresh kale from the garden and tore it in small pieces from the stem. I then ran it on frozen drink again. After that, I ran it at high for a few minutes.

I tasted it again. It was so chunky it was ridiculous. The greens were not blended in nearly well enough.

Then I took out the other very old blender and divided the blended drink in half. I processed each half in each blender for the exact same amount of time on high. When I tasted the Juicelady blended drink, I was amazed at how smooth it was. The Oster was just as chunky as it had been before.

We are pretty skilled at using kitchen appliances and this one really does fall short. I have to say I was not expecting to be THIS disappointed.

WHAT IS THIS BLENDER FOR?
This would make great smoothies with frozen fruits that are not highly seeded or with tough skins like mangoes, bananas, apples, etc. Raspberries, currants, and other fruits with seeds would not be a good choice. The frozen drink program does a decent job with the frozen fruits if you add enough liquid with it. Chunky salsas, and cold soups might be fine in this as well.

WHAT IS THE BLENDER NOT GOOD FOR?
If you intend to use chunky veggies like carrots, you will probably end up with chunks in your drink or other item. Fibrous greens like kale and collard will not blend smoothly in this. If you like chunks, then it will probably be okay.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I was very disappointed with this blender. We really loved the Oster we had years ago, but this one was just not up to what it should be for the price paid for it. The lit up display is great, the programs have a nice touch to them, but if they don't really do the job, what is the point? Low and medium speeds seem so weak they don't seem as if they will do much of anything.

Our old blender with ORIGINAL BLADES did a better job than this one did. And when it comes to green smoothies, it just does not come close to the Vitamix models of today. If you are considering having constant smoothies with greens, lots of raw food prep, I would highly suggest you skip this and move toward the Vitamix, or perhaps [[ASIN:B01M68CDM9 Blender HANMEIUS Multi Speed Electric Commercial Power Blender High Professional Performance Processor Mixer Nutrition Blender for Ice, Smoothies, Vegetable, Fruit]] which is a newer release to the market that seems to be a better price at the time of this review.

Because this does do simple fruit smoothies well and basic watery substances well, I am giving this two stars. It is not a total failure. For what we want it for, however, it just does not seem strong enough to pull its weight.

When I first purchased my 3 TB MBL some time ago I was quite pleased. Network access, remote access, even an android app. In short, everything my DLink had plus the app and a nicer look on the shelf. I used it extensively for pulling up photos on my cell phone when I was bored as well as to store my most important files. I didn't back them up, a back-up drive is something I kept saying I would add later...

14 months later (note the 12 month warranty had just expired) the drive stopped being accessible over the network. I spent a week and at least 40 hours of my time going back and forth with tech support by e-mail and trying every option they could offer, and the result was that they deemed the unit broken. They said that the unit can not be opened because that would break the drive inside, and they said that they can't fix it. They "kindly" offered me a referral to one of several companies that give them a kick back for data recovery services. Incidentally, I asked two for pricing by e-mail and they didn't respond.

So I took the unit apart and bought a new unit and took that one apart and swapped the drives. Neither one worked. After talking to support again it turns out that WD didn't want these to be upgradable because if they were upgradable you could buy a cheap drive instead of a new unit so they code each board to the drive that will be in it. TO make matters worse, they encoded the drive in a Linux format that no known version of Linux can translate. Attaching it to my Linux system I couldn't mount it using any utility. Several Linux recovery programs couldn't do anything either.

Okay, having told you why I will never buy a WD NAS again, I should now tell you how to fix this if you have the same problem that I do: DiskInternals makes a program called Linux Reader. That's right, Linux can't read the drive but a program designed to read Linux drives from within Windows can! Recovering the data to a drive is time consuming though. I tried it all at once but that froze after a few days. Then I tried one major directory at a time and that worked better. But recovering nearly 3 TB of data has taken a very long time! I'm about 3 MONTHS into the recovery effort and I have about 400 GB remaining. After starting on my wife's computer because mine is a laptop and causing a few crashes and a lot of delays I finally had to pull out an older computer and set it up just to run this program.

If anyone has the same problem and can't get this solution to work, I'll do my best to help if you simply reply to this review and give me all the details. If anyone is considering buying a WD NAS, I want to encourage you to buy a DLink model 323 (I think the 325 is the current version but it is missing some features so I'd get an older one) instead. I've had that thing running for 5 years without a glitch!

Years ago, I lived with a roommate who was a nurse. Once she came home with a nasty stomach flu and got terribly sick. She said she had caught a particularly bad strain of it and I watched uneasily as she spent three days in bed, rising only to throw up and such. Since our apartment was small and we shared cups and dishes, I knew it was just a matter of time before I got her flu.

Luckily I stopped at the drugstore and asked the pharmacist if there was anything to take at the first sight of a cold. My throat had started to hurt and I knew what was coming. He recommended Airborne. Until then I had regarded it warily, thinking it was some kind of snake oil. The folksy cartoon packaging didn't reassure me. I read the ingredients. I felt it couldn't hurt but I had low expectations of it.

What a miracle. I took it for three days after that, and other than a slightly sore throat and minor cough, I felt I had dodged a bullet. I never got nauseous or had to take time off from work. Although I still developed a nagging cough, I felt that Airborne helped me skip over the worst parts of my friend's illness. My nursing friend also a bad cough as she was recovering, but it seemed to take her several days to reach the same stage I was on.

My biggest mistake ever was a time when I had a severe respiratory infection and I forgot to take Airborne and nip it in the bud. Instead I let it run its natural course and it spread to my left ear, which has now left me with tinnitus. I sometimes kick myself for not taking Airborne the minute I started feeling sick that time, I might have prevented the medical complication I suffer to this day.

I can't seem to re-rate this review, but having had the thing for several months now, I've run across the same problem Shelley Ryan had with it: it doesn't actually get the oil hot enough!!! As it comes without a thermometer, you have to check the temps yourself, and I guess I'm going to have to try "Closer"'s approach of stirring the oil. As pointed out elsewhere, 375F is the recommended temp for frying, and some recipes call for a first fry at a lower temperature, which is VERY DIFFICULT with the ProFry's trial-and-error setting.

The Presto Profry requires a gallon of oil in it's square, removable reservoir. It comes with two mesh fry-baskets that fold up for easy storage. They'll sit side-by-side within the reservoir which is VERY convenient for, say, leaving the battered chicken to fry for 18 minutes while frying the onion rings for 5 and switching 'em out for some broccoli.

The temperature guage is indeed not accurate and one annoying note is that when it reaches its target heat the LED turns off, so at a casual glance you wouldn't know the fryer was on, containing oil at a temperature of 3??F. Once the oil has cooled it is RELATIVELY easy to lift the reservoir out of its housing and pour off the reusable portion of the oil. It has a lid with slots to accomodate the basket-handles when the lid is on the fryer.

I find the ProFry a LOT more convenient to use than the old deep fry pot on the stovetop, but obviously it takes up some counter space. If it turns out that there is some way of increasing the fry temperature, I'd rate it highly.

I was definitely taken in by the commercials and rave reviews here. I have two short hair cats that shed like the dickens and an ancient 85$ Hoover I purchased at K-mart one desperate day in college when family was coming to visit. My Hoover finally gave up the ghost and now that I have a real job I thought I would splurge a little. Is the Dyson better than the ancient $85 Hoover - definitely yes. Many hundreds of dollars worth? Not so sure. I've had this vacuum for about two months now.

Pros
-Like everyone has said, the vacuum has great suction. When I vacuum my 1,000 sq feet of carpet, I generally empty the bin twice. It's filled mostly with loose cat hair and kitty litter dust.

-What's in the bin is visible. It's rather satisfactory to see all the junk you are pulling off your carpet and into the trash.

-The handle at the top of the bin is well positioned to carry the vacuum up and down stairs. Or, to hold on to while vacuuming the stairs.

-The cord hinge twist thing is great. The cord hinge on the top, swivels so you can dump off the entire cord with one motion. It is nice to not have to unwrap the cord for every use.

-The high quality plug. This plug is built tough. Every other vacuum I've ever has a wimpy plug that gets quickly bent after being pulled out of the wall wrong.

-The pet attachment thingy with the moving roller. It does work fairly well on steps or upholstered furniture. Too bad I have to use the accordion hose to use it. I've given up using this on the stairs and now just carry the vacuum and use the regular upright part to do stairs. It's very heavy but not as much of a struggle.

-Emptying the bin is very, very easy. It can be a bit messy because of all the loose dust and cat hair so I tend to bring a small trash container into the living room, empty the bin into it and they quickly re vacuum the area.

-Hand cleanable filters. I haven't had to do it yet but I'm very much looking forward to the hand cleanable filters.

Cons
-This vacuum is NOT lightweight. I have NO IDEA what they are comparing this to when they say this. Perhaps there are gold vacuums out there I've never heard of?? My old Hoover which had the same variety of attachments was much lighter. My mom has an Oreck which must be half the weight. Is it too heavy?? Not really but it borders on it. I just feel the ads were deceptive here.

-The attachment hose is very awkward to use. Its accordion design pulls back on itself - that is, it always is trying to fold back into to its smallest possible configuration. So, to use it, I must always be actively pulling against it to keep it extended. This is exhausting and awkward. It will also pull the vacuum right over on its side. Or down the steps. Which is not just annoying but pretty dangerous considering how heavy the thing is. Most vacuums have awkward hoses. I'd put this one down as slightly more awkward than most.

-The plastic extension piece is too long. It's around three feet long so it is beyond awkard to use to clean off furniture or reach around in small spaces - say behind a toilet or around the cusions of a sofa. It took me a few weeks before I realized you could remove it when using the hose. This is a little better but without something firm to hold onto, the accordion hose is even harder to wrestle with as it tries to shorten itself back to its original size. Sigh!

-Switching back and forth between the attachment and regular upright vacuuming is awkward. I keep figuring I'll get better at it with practice but not so far. I have to beat back the plastic extension piece and then aim it into the holder - which always misses a few times. It always gets locked against the hose at the wrong place, etc.

-Angle end attachment is not angled. Ummmm... What's up with this?? There's nothing to use for cleaning baseboards, etc that can get in nice and close with corners.

-Combo angle attachment brush thing is useless. Since the brush is on the non-angled angled thing, I can't use the angle attachment to into tight spaces like between seat cushions or behind a book shelf or what not.

Neither here nor there:
-The ball. It's fun to look at but it doesn't really do anything for the vacuum. Yes, it could turn tight corners but only if you could actually steer the bottom portion of the vacuum. Since I'm only holding the handle, I'm still stuck doing the standard back and forth of a usual vacuum. The ball also won't fit under a bed so you can't sneak the vacuum very far under anything like I could with my old Hoover or my mom's Oreck.

-No light. I love the light on my mom's Oreck. Since I don't think it really helps anything cleaning wise the lack of one just makes the vacuum less cool but it doesn't take anything away.

-It's just a loud as any other vacuum - no better, no worse.

-Too big to fit on a stair. All vacuums are but I wish one day they'd invent a good one that could safely fit on the stairs and still work as an all around the house regular vacuum.

So basically, It works fine as upright vacuum but using the attachments is really difficult and they are poorly designed and poorly thought out. I think Dyson clearly knows a lot about suction and self promotion (their ads are fantastic!!) but a lot less about attachments. I'd recommend staying away from this model and look for Dyson with a different attachment design.

July 2012 update:

I'm really regretting this purchase now. The hose is so hard to use that now I rarely do - which means dust, cat hair and dead bugs are accumulating along my baseboards, in corners and under furniture. All Dyson had to do was put a spring in the hose that was less strong. So simple but they didn't bother. It would not have even have costed any more money - I'm guessing less strong springs actually cost less. It's like they never bothered having real women test this thing. All their money was paid to their advertising company. Grrrrr....

I'm also sick of hauling this thing up and down the stairs - it is too dang heavy. I'm thinking of buying another, lighter vacuum for the upstairs.

Having had plenty of paraffin wax treatments in spas and salons, I had high hopes for these gloves and being able to save some cash and do it myself at home. Unfortunately, it's not as easy as I thought.

The gloves are bulky and large which made me think that my hands would fit but also realized that I would need my husband's help to get the second one on. While I did require help to put the second glove on (putting them both on yourself is near impossible), they weren't as large as they first appeared and my hands barely fit inside (I was actually surprised I didn't rip them) and so the fit was tight and uncomfortable.

I heated them in the microwave as instructed but the wax melted in a weird way in both gloves. Glove 1 - the wax melted so much that, while I was able to get my hand in and smush/spread the wax around my fingers, it was an odd watery texture. Glove 2 - the wax hardly melted at all, making it so lumpy and hard in places that my fingers didn't even fit into the finger slots all the way and I didn't get as much full coverage from the wax since it wouldn't spread at all.

Despite these difficulties, I did manage to wear them for the recommended 10 minutes (with the aforementioned assistance of my husband). Removing them was yet another challenge... my hubby held the glove itself while I slid my hand out, trying to keep the wax inside the glove. Now, anyone who has had a wax dip knows exactly what "sweeping" maneuvers I was doing along my fingers but I must say that these techniques didn't work with these gloves. I think it comes down to the weird consistency of the wax. Needless to say, I got wax everywhere but inside the gloves. It was a mess.

Once off, I tried to clip them shut with the included clip and this is where yet another challenge presented itself... the clip is not as wide as the openings on the gloves so it is not possible to clip the gloves closed using the included clip. Since these gloves are claimed to be multi-use, I just laughed at this point.

Bottom line.. these gloves are too much of a hassle. They are too difficult to use, the wax must be bottom of the line grade and the included clip was not made to fit the gloves in the same kit rendering this kit a one-time-use deal. Oh! And my hands didn't feel any more moisturized than before I began this entire ordeal. These are a definite no go for me and I will not be recommending it. Just save enough to buy two of these kits and go and treat yourself to a real wax treatment at your local spa or salon. Trust me.

My wife and I have been taking supplements for years and that has no doubt helped me get to the age I am. We thought that we had all the supplements covered -- that is without going to extremes -- until my daughter and her husband called one night and recommended that we add 400 mg of Zinc to our regimen. After looking at the Zinc content in the supplements we were already taking, it was obvious that I needed about 300 mg more than what I was using. My wife gets most of hers through her treatment for macular degeneration but I don't have that problem.

Once I started looking for large doses of Zinc it became obvious that the most common dose was 50 mg with 100 mg coming in a distant second. After researching the various doses available and reading lots of reviews, I settled on this Nutrivein product. I knew going into this product that Zinc potentially has several unpleasant side effects for different people. The recommended daily amount of Zinc is 8 mg for women and 11 mg for men.

I knew that adding this much Zinc to my daily regimen could potentially cause problems for me. These include: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, as well as kidney and stomach damage. So it's important that you check with your physician before taking large doses of Zinc. Many people are intolerant of such a large dose and some simply can't "stomach it". No problems for me.

This supplement is low-dose Omega 3s, garlic bulb extract, Gotu Kola, Pine Bark Extract, and Olive Leaf Extract. I do not know what these have to do with keeping your cardiovascular system healthy, and I cannot imagine the science behind these is strong.

If you want Omega 3s, just take fish oil. It has significant science behind it, although it isn’t really a supplement for heart health. It is more for brain health. If you want the benefits of olives, eat olives or olive oil rather than supplement with the minuscule quantity of olive leaf extract found in these pills, which will likely do nothing for you.

The marketing says these ingredients have human clinical studies proving their effectiveness, which is overstating reality. Their Web site for this product links to Examine for the science, which is a great formerly-free Web site that now requires a subscription. Their science link for the Omega 3s in this is for fish oil, not AvailOm Omega 3s.

I looked for research showing how Pine Bark Extract helps with cardiovascular health, and the first human study I found proved that it provides no cardiovascular benefit and the authors mentioned that the previous studies were flawed.

The AvailOm they are claiming is more bioavailable is being compared to AHA, not to DHA or EPA. This is a straw-man comparison.

This company does an excellent job of marketing, and they make a pill with basic ingredients look fancier than it is. You can get much more Omega 3s from other vendors for less money. The only reason to get this pill that I can see is if you are a sucker for slick marketing.

They put the lab test results on their Web site, which I give them credit for. They also offer a money-back guarantee, which is great.

The source ingredients are from China.

I take fish oil every day for brain health. I sometimes supplement with Gotu Kola and Pine Bark Extract, but not for heart health.

At the time of this review the listing has a picture of a temperature chart showing that the pad goes from 86 to 140 degrees from level 1 to level 10. At the lower settings, it barely gets above room temperature in my 68 degree house.

I contacted the seller and while he was generous in offering me a replacement (I did not accept), the seller did give away that per the factory, the whole batch of this model, because of the large size of the pad itself, can not heat up to the stated specifications. The seller did add that “in the next shipment, heating efficiency and speed will be improved.” I would imagine that they will then make that next shipment a new listing on Amazon, possibly marked as a new and improved model. If they do not, it will be impossible to tell which pad you are getting, the one with the controller that is not powerful enough for the size of the pad, or the improved model.

The listing currently says in the Q&A section regarding laying and sitting on it that “Yes the large size heating pad is update Technology in 2022 which is Reclinable and sittable” but the instructions for the pad and the box for the pad I received say you can NOT sit on it and NOT to put it under any blankets. However, I do find that if I am using it, if I put a heavy blanket over it, it will capture the heat and after an hour or longer, it will build up enough heat to register in the low 90s with my temperature gun. With this method, the pad does show minimal usefulness. Because of the warnings on the box and instructions, I would never leave it turned on under anything unless I am actively present to monitor for any issues (the fear would be overheating, but I don’t think there’s any way this device would have enough power to do that regardless).

Finally, the material of the pad is nice and soft. It is large, as advertised and the controller has a nice lockout feature in that you have to hold a button for three seconds to turn it on or off. This comes in three pieces. The yellow silicone cover on the handle, the frame itself with the egg well, and the silicone "bowl or rim." 

After washing for first use, submerge this poacher in boiling water up to rim of poacher and pour egg from a prep bowl into the egg well once the water begins to swirl. Cook for 2-4 minutes, drain, and serve.

It seems easy (see first four photos for instructions) but it is not.  First of all, when the water was ready, I poured the egg into the poacher and after a few seconds white foam (from the egg white) coagulated in the water. Once the egg was cooked, I gently lifted this from the pot. However, the yellow silicone handle kept sliding off so I had to keep re-attaching it. I finally squeezed it tightly while lifting the handle so it woud not fall off again. After the "egg well" drained as I lifted it from the pot, I turned over the poacher to release the egg.

Good luck. The egg is stuck relatively solid to the egg well. Only the yolk and top part of the egg white slipped out. I had to use a spoon to extricate the rest and it left some concrete residue behind.

I wanted to do another egg but the previous event clogged all the vents in the poacher.  It took me a couple of hours of soaking the poacher in Dawn Platinium and scrubbing it for about 15 minutes to remove the "concrete" residue. Not only was this a tremendous amout of work but it was not easy to remove the silicone rim from the poacher for washing and re-assembling.

In summary, this is an absolutely awful poacher. It would be best to just crack the egg into boiling water with vinegar and then removing it with a slotted spoon. I am glad I used a non-stick pan or I would have been scrubbing that into the wee hours.

THE VERDICT - This gets an F minus. Use only if you want to spend hours extracting one poached egg and working on the cleanup.

As someone who works with cameras for a living, I tend to occasionally misplace/lose my lens caps. Having a one-size-fits-all backup like this claims to be, is therefore intriguing to me.
What I found however, is that this fits alright for smaller sized primes (such as those with a front element of 52mm), but a lot of my zooms or larger primes with bigger front elements are difficult or impossible to fit over. Rear cap was also somewhat of a hit-or-miss; I own E-mount, EOS, Nikon F, Minolta A-mount and Micro4/3 lenses, and none of them are too large in their rear element, but some lenses get wide right after the mount and won't allow a cover like this to squeeze over easily. Some of the smaller primes, especially pancake lenses like the Canon 40mm STM, really can't fit both a front and rear "cap" like this since the entire lens would be engulfed in one end or the other.
On top of all that, even if it DOES fit over your lens, I'm cynical as to how how useful it really is. The purpose of a lens cap is to protect the glass from two things: getting dirty and getting damaged. For starters, the material is soft and won't prevent a hard object collision. I'm not exactly willing to test that theory but considering I can press in and feel the glass through the cover, I'm guessing a hard object in your camera bag could still hit it and crack/shatter/damage it. Perhaps the rubber would soften the blow, but a real lens cap would prevent any blow from happening in the first place!
For dust and debris protection, perhaps it is a little useful, however this sort of material tends to attract a lot of static cling. Just leaving it in my gear bag for a bit, I'm finding dust and hair clinging to it like a balloon. Now, it is possible that means the dust/debris will stick to the cap and not your lens, which is useful, however it doesn't give me a lot of confidence to see stuff stuck to the thing I'm about to use to protect my lens from more of that stuff.

I suppose it's good as a backup in my gearbag in case I lose another lens cap and want something to keep dust off it until I get a replacement, but otherwise I'd strongly recommend getting a proper front and end cap for your lenses.

I'm not brave enough to fully submerge my iPhone in water to test this case, but I did test it several times with various proxies, which did come out dry. When I put a paper towel (chosen largely at random, but also because it seemed a small amount of water would be immediately obvious) inside the case and held it under a tap, the paper towel was still dry when I took it out, which is very promising. I even ran water over the top of the case, where it closes, and the seal held, not allowing any water to penetrate to my paper towel cell phone stand-in. I repeated the test with the paper instruction card that came with the case with a similarly promising result, but I'm still just not ready to dunk my very expensive phone.

In addition to its effectiveness in my kitchen-lab product test, I was also very happy that my phone fits into this case while still inside the bulky Otter Box case I already use. This is perfect because it's much more convenient to stick both the phone and the case into the second case for added protection and water proofing than to switch cases.

The reason I wanted to try this case is not because I plan to start submerging my phone in water, but because I spend a lot of time at pools as a caregiver and really need to have my phone on me. I wanted something that would keep my phone safe from getting wet if it were splashed, if I accidentally set it down on a wet chair, or if I need to pick it up with wet hands. I'm also terrified that I will actually just drop it into the pool because I drop it all the time, hence the Otter Box defender case. It's great that I can keep the protection my phone already has and quickly add this over top of it as a back up.

Update:
After using the case for a while I took several stars off my rating. First, while initially it seemed that the case wasn't affecting the usability of my phone, after using it properly (**trying to use it**) several times at the pool, I've realized that it's nearly impossible to type or do anything but the most basic functions with the phone in the case. You can see the screen okay, so reading things on the phone is possible. As for how water proof it is... I don't trust it that much. The top part actually fell apart apart, and while all the pieces just sort of clipped back together, I really wouldn't trust submerging it without retesting it each time. However, I am still using it. I stick my phone in here while I'm at the pool and only take it out occasionally, and feel more comfortable if it gets splashed. That's splashed with a few drops of water, not dunked or soaked.

When I first opened the package of this Fellowes I-Spire Series Monitor Lift (9311101), I was not impressed with what looked like a small version of a cheap plastic bed tray with curved edges. The only thing I like about it, is that it is fairly small (just under 20 inches wide by about 8 1/2 inches deep) and fits on my already crowded desk that holds my computer tower, monitor, keyboard, printer, scanner, extra USB port hub, surge protector and speakers. I didn't like a lot of things about the design, like what is up with the curved edges- it appears to be wasted space and the fact that you can't put the keyboard underneath the lift as it is too narrow. I thought this was one of the worst designs until I saw these at my local library.

I was so shocked to see 50 of these monitor lifts in my library! My library has 2 computer rooms- one section has 30 computer monitors, the other more private room has 20 computer monitors. Of course I was not only surprised to see what I thought were poorly designed cheap plastic lifts, but I was curious enough to ask why the library got rid of the larger metal flat lifts and replaced them with these cheaper looking curved ones. The librarian told me the wider flat metal lifts had a huge problem with sagging in the middle. She said they always end up sagging eventually, making them useless. She told me the curved edges of this Fellowes Monitor Lift actually are designed this way to eliminate the sagging middles. The librarian also told me the old flat metal monitor lifts had adjustable legs, which always came loose and when the monitor lift was lifted or moved for cleaning, the legs would always fall off. I had no clue that the larger, flatter monitor lifts had these issues.

I learned a lot by speaking with someone who knows what is best for a row of monitors that need to be made to eye level for the public. This Fellowes Monitor Lift is curved to avoid middle sagging. It has no legs that can come loose or fall off. It is made of easy to dust or clean plastic. It has openings on the bottom on all 4 sides for easy storage of all your cords- but not your keyboard. The lift height brings your monitor up almost 3 1/2 inches, making better eye level viewing and less neck, shoulder and back pain for you. This monitor lift has rubber on the 4 bottom corners for stability, so it doesn't slide or move around.

The main thing you need to know is to make certain your monitor base is no wider than 12 inches and not deeper than 8 inches, so it fits on the curved base. [[VIDEOID:552730d92212a2c0a38ed65a0a9e1972]] This is the 53rd BP monitor that I have tried and ordered through Amazon either via purchase or the Vine program. Almost every single monitor takes my BP within a few points of each other and this one operates within range of my gold star monitors.  This monitor holds a total of 198 readings if using all two user modes. The LCD Display is small but easy to read. There are two power options of either four AAA batteries (included) or a micro-USB cable (NOT included). There is an average feature after two readings and not three like the manual says. The date and time settings are in 24-hour clock only (military time). The cuff size is small (22-32cm). There is also voice broadcast mode. This has an irregular heartbeat indicator. This monitor is quirky and it would not work the first time (see video). I was ready to throw this out. I then tried my own micro-USB cable and got it to work. I then put the batteries in again and it worked. However, I am not confident in this monitor as there are others that are better.

INCLUDED IN THE PACKAGE
- One BP unit

- One BP User Manual

- One small cuff

- Four AAA batteries

- One cloth case

FEATURES
- Up to 99 numbers can be stored for each of two users in memory.

- Date and time settings are available.

- Setting the date and time or selecting the user is a matter of using the set and memory buttons per the instruction manual but memory deletion is quirky.

- The LCD Display readout is small 

- The cuff is small 22 to 32 cm (8.66 to 12.598 inches)

- It has a voice broadcast mode.

- The user guide is decent.

- Accuracy is good and compares with the BP range taken on my two 5-star gold standard monitors.

- Switching user modes is a two button process by pressing SET for three seconds (when power is off) and then MEM to switch to the other user.

- It displays an average after two readings even though the manual says three readings.

NEGATIVES
- The unit would not work or turn off at first.

- The display and cuff are small.

To take my blood pressure, I affixed the cuff around my LEFT arm with my palm turned up. I made sure my arm was at heart level and my feet were flat on the floor. Then I pressed start and after a little bit, I had my reading. I pressed stop to turn off the unit. The systolic and diastolic pressures and pulse are displayed.

In summary, this BP monitor is accurate and within range of my two go to monitors but the unit has its drawbacks and I do not trust it. Blood pressure is never the same from moment to moment, so it is expected to get variable readings within a certain range even over several minutes. It is important for a user to learn how to take their BP to get an accurate reading or it may appear that a monitor is not working when, in fact, it is user error. There are many great videos online that can help teach this.

The current price of $29.99 ($39.99 minus $10) is outrageous for this monitor, especially since it is so lackluster and has a small display and cuff.

For those who are interested, I attached some notes about several of my most favorite 5-star monitors. These monitors I consider outstanding for their features compared to all the others I tested. I listed two 4-star monitors because they have unique features such as Spanish speaking or Bluetooth. Each one of these monitors is accurate and I would highly recommend any of them.

That only works if it is turned on. Accuracy is spot on, which is atypical of wrist monitors. (5 stars)

[[ASIN:B01AFQK85K HealthSmart Upper Arm BP Monitor]] – This is great if a talking monitor in both English and Spanish is needed. It stores 120 readings between 2 users. In addition to battery operation, it comes with an AC adapter, two very flimsy cuffs, and a case. If the cuffs were better, this would be my favorite arm monitor. (4 stars)

[[ASIN:B08HK71G16 Teyiyes Digital Upper Arm BP Monitor]] -This is a great monitor with a large cuff, two power sources (4 AAA batteries or A/C cable), and 2 user capacity 90 memory capacity for each. (4.5 stars)

(Both are 4 stars)

I have used drip systems many times over the years and find them an excellent way to make sure your plants or garden receive regular scheduled watering at the appropriate times of the day.

I plant my garden in a mixture of raised beds and large pots. This allows me great control over the soil composition, drainage, sunlight and watering.

I could tell immediately after opening the box the components are as cheaply made as they possibly can be - and I can confirm this after using this set for the last six weeks.

The timer is absolute junk. The face will not stay on nor will the batteries remain in place. Due to being stubborn I tried gluing the face to the connection points with an outdoor rated glue and electrical taping the batteries. While I managed to get those issues resolved it will not keep accurate time whatsoever. This was the first part to go in the trash. I already had a replacement.

All of my raised beds and pots are located close together so running the tubing wasn’t any big deal. Having done it before I knew the tubing layout that worked best last time.

After having everything set up I turned it on and it worked as it should. I never run these systems under high water pressure as I’ve learned from previous experience this leads to the tubes uncoupling.

During the second watering of the second day this set was in use I experienced the first tube coming free. This is not uncommon as the tubes have to be fit really snugly into the fittings. I replaced it and it popped free within 10 min. So I replaced it and added a zip tie. It held... The following day I had 2 more come free. Same routine.

Over the last 6 weeks I’ve added zip ties to every coupled location and even with those a few have come free! The tubing is just cheap and stretches even under minimal pressure.

I may trash this entire system before this growing season is over. Currently I’m still trying to make it work but it’s only because I’m stubborn.

This is absolutely not a product I would ever recommend.

I'm going to be one of the few dissenting opinions on this screen protector. Here is my little saga with the Armorsuit Shield -

When I got my brand new S7 edge I wanted it really protected. I have never used a screen protector on a phone before - I've also never paid so much for a phone before!! I had a case and the Armorsuit before I bought the phone!! I put the screen protector on just after getting the phone all set up and ready to go.

The application was really easy. I love wet application covers (used them for my fitbit) as they are so much more forgiving than the dry application. You can really take your time and get good alignment. This protector is great as far as the size and cut out spaces. It fits perfectly and leaves the tiniest of margins along the edge to prevent your case from lifting the corners.

That's where the love ends. After several days the screen still looked hazy. A slight rainbow (the plastic film) was always present on my screen and was particularly annoying when a lot of white was present on the screen (like when reading). Any tiny bubbles did disappear but it never got clear.

After about 2 weeks - YEP- the screen had lifted up and rolled back on itself. It was a mess! Lint and crud stuck to it. I removed the Armorsuit and tried to pick all the crap off, but a good bit remained and the smudges never really came out. I also noticed that my screen was not as responsive after putting the Armorshield back on again. I think messing up the adhesive reduced the sensitivity. It was a real pain - but something I didn't notice when the screen protector was first applied. I think this was from removing and replacing it. After a few days I just pulled it off. As far as this being "reusable", don't bank on it. If you take it off for any reason - stuff will stick to the back side and you'll never get it clean again.

To save my phone I do want to at least try another protector - but I'll be trying out another brand this time.

I had to replace the phone on my ATT plan ( Nokia Mural ) because the battery life was horrible, it dropped calls, would not receive calls and the menu navigation was awful.

I am not interested in a smart phone. My top priorities are battery life, call quality and ease of use. I could also care less about a camera in a phone. I also carry my phone in my pocket so the size and shape of this phone is important. For the 2 weeks I have owned this phone it has met all of these criteria. I went 3 days before the first charge and that was after playing with all the phones features like WLAN, bluetooth camera and media player and I still had battery left. The call quality is superb, people talking to me on the other end have also noticed the difference, no dropped callls so far. The ring volume is EXCELLENT! The main screen and goto menus are totally customizable so if you don't find this phone easy to use it is your own fault. The resistive touch makes navigation easy. The screen is also very clear and the picture quality is excellent. Texting uses the traditional key pad and utilizes the touch feature for special charachters. This phone is thin and the back is rounded so it carries well in my pocket, sometimes I forget it is there.

Now for the extra features. The camera takes pretty awful pictures but I find that true with most phones. Flash photography on this thing produces incredibly washed out colors. I the WLAN feature is great!, the default browser is very poor but it also comes with Opera Mini web browser pre-installed and that works surprisingly well. This does not surf the web as well as a "smart" phone but it is certainly tolerable. One of my favorite features is the * button can be held down for 3 seconds to turn on the camera flash for a flashlight. Love it! So far the software support from Nokia is poor because the phone is so new. There is no ActiveSync which I think is true for most phone. SUPL location, which uses tower triangulation to find your location, is available but I have not found an app that it works with yet. The java google maps does not support the touch screen. It comes with a built in mail app which support gmail. The is no plugin yet for Apple iSync. Hopefully there will be better software choices the longer this phone is out. The music player is relatively good, decent sound and a regular sized headphone jack is awesome. I also appreciate the ability to charge with both the Nokia barrel charger and micro usb.

I own an ipod touch which senses electrical conductivity, this phone differs in that it uses resistive touch which senses pressure. It is not as sensitive but has the advantage of not exposing a glass surface ( possibly more durable ) and you could still use it with gloves on. Once you get use to using the touch on this phone it goes smooth. It seems to work best with your thumb.

I would recommend this phone to anyone who likes to use their phone as a phone.

Garnier really knows how to take wonderful care of hair. I've been using various Garnier products for years and years. Shampoos, conditioners, leave-in, wave/curl sprays. Once again, Garnier delivers yet another fabulous shampoo + conditioner!

Hibiscus + Shea focuses on curls. I wash my hair daily. I RARELY skip using conditioner. The consistency of this shampoo is silky and creamy. I love it. An amount roughly the size of a nickel is sufficient for my shoulder length, thick hair. It is so easy to work through my hair and it lathers immediately. As I rinsed it and ran my fingers through my hair I could already feel how soft, silky and tangle free my hair was. I decided to skip the conditioner; the shampoo had worked SO well I wanted to see how my hair looked using shampoo only. (Again, I stress that I VERY rarely skip conditioner, so this was practically unheard of for me ) After towel drying my hair, I combed it and let it air dry as I always do. In the end, my natural curls and waves looked great; they were soft and smooth and free of the usual flyaways. There was a bit of a decrease in how wavy/curly my hair normally is but I was still impressed with the result and didn't regret skipping the conditioner. The following night, I used both the shampoo + conditioner. The consistency of the conditioner is far thicker than the shampoo. After having it sit on my hair for about 5 minutes, I rinsed the conditioner and did so without issue. As with the shampoo, I could feel how soft and tangle free my hair was during the rinse. Again, I towel dried my hair and then allowed it to air dry. When dry, my waves and curls were fantastic. No flyaways. Soft, shiny and a bit of a bounce. And my hair smelled GREAT! There is a scent to both the conditioner and shampoo though its very light. But its not long lasting, unfortunately. (IDK if its just me but my hair rarely holds a shampoo/conditioner scent for long)

Though I havent' tried it, I want to mention this conditioner can be used as a leave in.

I'm not the least bit surprised how well this duo worked in my hair. Garnier knows what they're doing when it comes to hair care. I'm more than satisfied with the results this combo delivered and absolutely recommend it to those with curly/wavy hair.

*FYI...this product comes with a sample of Garnier's Miracle Nectar Honey leave in. I've been using this leave in on and off since last year and it works beautifully!

When I was a child I had earaches on occasion.  Actually, I had them more often that I probably should have.  We had an above-ground pool that I spent hours in during the summer and I believe I developed swimmer's ear from it.  My mother did not believe in taking children to the doctor for every complaint and when I told her my ear hurt when I swallowed, she would warm up a small amount of sweet almond oil and drop it in my ear, then take a piece of a cotton ball, stuff that in my ear and tell me to keep my head tilted for a little while so the warm oil had time to work.  Believe it or not, that old-fashioned remedy worked at least for me and my painful ear.  So, I don't suffer them much any more, but I still DO get earaches, I took a small amount of the oil in small glass jar and set it in very warm water to warm the oil, then used an eyedropper to drop some of the oil in my ear.  Just like my mother did, I took a piece of cotton ball and plugged my ear, keeping my head tilted until I felt it move a bit deeper in the ear canal.  You know, it felt the same as when I was a kid!  So, for me, sweet almond oil is my earache remedy and I love it.

That clasp can be removed by prying up one side when it is off the container and the clasp is down but not locked. One end of the clasp has a slot whereas the other end has only a hole. Reassembly is the reverse - put the hole in the clasp over the nub in the container, close the clasp but don't lock it onto a container, and press the slotted end down over the other nub until it clicks into place. [ I swear someone must have read my review of the Hamilton Beach Coffee Brewstation from 2012 when I wrote that was how I removed the coffee maker's lid - by cutting a slot in one side of the lid's hinge. ]
I was under the impression it was tempered glass but it is flexible plastic.

PROS

1. Even though this device is manufactured by a Chinese company, the manual is well written in good English with mostly correct grammar and punctuation (which I have rarely found to be the case with items manufactured in China). It is very detailed and contains all crucial instructions.
2. A convenient carrying case is included, which can be hooked on a belt loop.
3. It comes with what the manual calls a "hanging rope," which is typically called a lanyard. It can be attached to the device and then hung around one's neck for easy access.
4. There is a well-lit, digital readout which shows the pulse rate and oxygen saturation percentage in large, red numbers.
5. Two AAA batteries are included, which are necessary to operate the device.
6. The price is quite affordable. Pulse oximeters vary wildly in cost, and this device is on the lowest end of that range.

CONS

1. The face of the device comes with a peel-off, protective film over it. I found it very difficult to detect. The only reason I even knew it was there was because it was scuffed. I was afraid the device was damaged until I suddenly recalled that my kitchen timers and my sports watch all came with a protective film over their face.
2. The identifying labels for the readout numbers, which tell you which number is the pulse rate and which number is the oxygen saturation percentage, are quite small. For a person with poor eyesight, it could lead to accidentally reading the numbers upside down and getting a false impression. For example, a reading of 98 when read upside down is 86, which is dangerously low.

GENERAL INFORMAION ON PULSE OXIMETERS

A pulse oximeter is a medical device that measures the saturation of oxygen in the blood and the pulse rate. Every time you go to a doctor’s office, they will place a pulse oximeter on your pointer finger at the same time they take your temperature and blood pressure. The normal range is 95-100%. If your reading drops to 92% or lower, the medical term for this is hypoxemia. Doctors take that condition quite seriously and might send you to the hospital for an overnight observation stay during which they would put you on supplementary oxygen. This is because the whole body needs oxygen to survive, and the brain and heart are especially vulnerable to damage from low oxygen levels.

APPLICATION OF PULSE OXIMETERS FOR COVID-19 (C19)

C19 can bring on a type of pneumonia which causes the lungs’ air sacs to fill with fluid or pus. In the early stages of this dangerous infection, the patient might not yet be experiencing difficulty breathing (such as panting or gasping), yet their blood oxygen levels are dangerously low. Patients can sometimes grow accustomed to gradually decreasing oxygen levels as the disease progresses, and, unfortunately, not go to the hospital until they are at the point of collapse. In such situations, their prognosis is much more precarious. A pulse oximeter, used routinely, can provide an early warning of this type of C19 danger, but it is crucial to utilize this device to take a reading both while walking around and while sitting. Doctors have found that some C19 patients may have a normal reading while sitting, but when walking around, their reading can drop to extremely dangerous levels.

CAVEATS FOR USE OF A PULSE OXIMETER

People who live at high altitudes might have typical, healthy readings in the low 90s. Thus, if you live at a high altitude, it is a good idea to take a baseline reading while you know you are healthy, so you can establish what is normal for you.

If your hands are cold when you use the device, it can cause you to get an inaccurate result.

Nail polish or fake nails can cause you to get an inaccurate result.

Be careful that you aren’t reading the device upside down, such that a 9 can look like a 6. (Which, as stated above, is a potential issue with this device, in particular.)

Had I not tried other massage balls in the past, I might have rated the 4 or 5 stars. However, I am disappointed in this set even though it works as designed. Others like this  [[ASIN:B092VC4GW1 one]] have a removable ball and this set does not have a removable ball.
In the giftable box are two small therapy balls with a base. The included instructions are written in broken English.

Due to the small size, this is easy to handle and is perfect for when I want to apply small and targeted hot or cold therapy to my neck, wrists, etc.

To use cold, I have to put the entire unit (base and all)  in the freezer for up to two hours. It got very cold in my freezer after only 30 minutes. I then roll it around the area needed.

To use hot and despite what the instructions say, I soak the ball in warm water for a few minutes.  What I do is place the "room temperature" ball with base in a Pyrex measuring cup and pour 185 degree water over it and let it soak for 10 minutes. The ball gets warm enough to use and stays that way for at least 10 minutes.

I tried this both ways and it works exceptionally well for small areas. However, the major problem is that the ball is not removable from the base. Therefore, it is hard to dry out and it is important not to switch balls and use the one I used for warmth in the freezer because it will be frozen in its base if it is still wet inside.

In summary, I rate this set 2 stars because the ball is NOT removable from the base and that is a BIG negative to me, especially for the hot implementation where the water from the base goes all over my body as I roll it around the area. The current price of $22.99 comes to $11.50 per ball.

I've had a RAID-5 array running with four of these Spinpoint F3 (HD103SJ) drives running since 2010. Over the past four years, I've had to replace SIX of these drives. That's right, I've owned a total of NINE of these, and I've replaced ALL of the original four.

Last year, I decided to stop wasting money on these and decided to just pay a little more for a different drive (WD Black), and today I'm running with three of the Samsung drives and one WD Black. Guess what? Two days ago, one of the remaining Samsung F3s started reporting a SMART failure. I ordered a replacement, and just today - TWO days after that Samsung F3 drive reported the SMART failure, a second Samsung F3 started reporting SMART failures, too.

So today, I've got three Spinpoint F3 drives left, two of which are about to die. That means in four years, I will have had 8 out of 9 of these drives die. None of them have lasted more than 1 1/2 years.

Just as a side note, I have another WD Black operating as my boot drive, a Caviar Green drive as a secondary data drive, and yet another WD Black as a final data drive (yes, my computer is a monstrosity). So of all of the drives in the system, ALL of them have held up for 2-4 years so far and the ONLY drives that have failed are these Spinpoint F3s.

Also, I've bought the drives from a variety of sources - NewEgg, Amazon, and MicroCenter, at different times, so it's not just like I happened to buy a bunch from a bad batch.

BOTTOM LINE: Don't waste your money. The high-star reviews are likely from new owners. Take it from someone who has tried these drives again and again for four years - they're junk.

This is a very comprehensive eyeglass repair kit. It covers a wide range of screws, and provides multiple sizes of replacement silicone nose pads. It comes with a workable set of screwdrivers and a pair of tweezers. The tool quality is not great, but they are good enough to get the job done. They are not, however, a set of tools that would stand up to any degree of heavy use. If you have a set of good precision screwdrivers you'll want to use those rather than the ones that come with the set.

The only significant issue I have with the set is the case. The latch broke the first time I opened the case. The dividers in the case are not well set, and doesn't provide secure arrangement of the screws (which are tiny and a major pain to pick up if dropped). Given the volume of screws and the fact that they are so tiny, this needs a better designed case that is more durable and less prone to spilling the contents. If you get this, open the case with as much care as possible to avoid the screws jumping out of their compartments, and put a rubber band around it to keep it closed when it's stored.

Given the importance of the case in keeping things organized, the included case is not at all ideal. Still, the set is very handy to have if you wear glasses since it's highly likely the glasses will need new pads or a replacement hinge screw, and this covers a lot of different sizes. Four stars (one star down due to the case).

This is a basic hypochlorous acid (HOCl). There's nothing wrong with that whatsoever since HOCl is a fantastic performer when it comes to sanitizing surfaces and getting rid of odors without having to resort to harsh chemicals. It has a mild chlorine-like scent and is fine for use on food contact surfaces. HOCl is great stuff!

However, this HOCl is lacking on a few key areas. It's rather pricey compared with similar options. Granted, it comes in an upscale (well, sort of upscale) bottle, but the solution itself is nothing new or unique. More importantly, it does not state the HOCl concentration on the bottle. Usually it's 0.02%, but I'd like to know if that is the case with this. Another key piece of info that's missing is the expiration date. HOCl has a shelf life (usually about 18 months). I have no idea when this was produced so I don't know how long it is good for. That's a key piece of info for a sanitizing agent.

While HOCl itself is a fantastic sanitizer, the lack of key info and the price compared with other HOCl options (that do state the concentration and expiration date) makes this a below average (2 star) product for me.

As an older person with some health issues, I've actually considered signing up for an emergency contact service so this came at a good time for me. But the biggest fear I've had with these systems is: Will it work as advertised if, heaven forbid, I fall or have some other emergency?

The smallest "personal alarm" device I've seen, Ripple is unique in several ways. It "piggybacks" via Bluetooth on your smartphone instead of having its own transmitter, and as such it is much smaller than similar emergency alarm systems since it doesn't have to carry extra electronics.

Set up is easy - install the smartphone app and then pair the device via Bluetooth. You need to make sure your phone allows Ripple to know your location, accept notifications, refresh in the background, and use cellular data in order to make sure you're covered. Also, if you have a non-emergency situation where you feel uncomfortable, you need to make sure your phone is close by as you'll get a callback or a text.

The only negative so far is there's no clear easy way to test that everything is set up properly without actually activating an alarm by clicking the button. I did that, just to see what the response would be and it was a little strange. After clicking the button once, I started timing to see how long it would take to get a callback. My phone rang at 2 minutes 44 seconds -- which seems a bit long to me, given the description that says "click once and immediately receive a call from Ripple Support." A lot can happen in almost 3 minutes. Also, after I answered the phone, I was asked if there was a problem, and before I could answer, we were disconnected. Another minute passed and I then received a text asking the same question and I explained that I was trying to test the system to make sure I had it set up correctly. It just seemed awkward that they wouldn't have something in the instructions on how to do this instead of waiting until there was a real emergency and then finding out that I mistyped something.

I intend to continue with the subscription program after the 1-month trial period is up. I think it probably works well enough to suit my needs. It will be most useful if I'm separated from my phone and experience a true emergency (a fall/etc.). Otherwise, if my phone is handy, I can just dial 911 myself. Overall, I'd give this 3.5 stars -- rounded up to 4.

Full disclosure. . .  I don’t have a “dirty job”.  So my clothes are typically “lightly soiled” at worst.  Having said that. . .  .These pods work great. I’ve tried several different brands and types of laundry detergent.  In the “old days” it was difficult to find any laundry detergent that didn’t suds too much.  Now all major brands have “he” detergent (high efficiency) which is supposed to work for front-load washers.  Not true.  Some of them still suds too much.  Too many suds means you have to keep rinsing and rinsing to get all of the soap out. . but. .  even worse. . . if it’s really bad, then the suds will start to come out of the detergent drawer and then you have a real mess.  With  Tide Pods there is not too much sudsing, as long as you use the pods for a “regular / large” load.  I do not recommend using the pods for a small or even medium load if you have a front-load washer.  I’ve done so and regretted it.  Hence, you will still need to have either some liquid or powder on hand.  Nonetheless, the pods work fine in both warm and cold water.

The drive was provided for review purposes.

I do not recommend this product. I cannot recommend any of the merchants who sell this product. And I cannot even recommend Amazon for purchasing this type of product. The "512gb" advertisement is fraud.

WHAT IS REALLY GOING ON???...MY COMPUTER SAYS 512GB, BUT THE DRIVE IS NOT FUNCTIONING CORRECTLY???
This is not a 512gb flash drive...in fact, while a few 512GB flash drives do exist, the going rate is starting around $300. If your computer shows the size of this drive as being 512gb, the drive has been "tricked" into displaying this inflated number. A Seller hacks the firmware code of the USB flash drive so that the drive is "tricked" into showing a size of 512gb, despite the fact that the drive's actual capacity is a fraction of this (in some cases less than 1% of the advertised size). The reason this drive is so slow is due to terrible quality flash memory, and the hacked firmware. In other words, use this drive and data loss is all but certain.

HOW DO I AVOID GETTING SCAMMED??? HOW DO I DETECT THESE SCAM FLASH DRIVES AND SD CARDS??? DOES AMAZON FULFILLMENT GUARANTEE A LEGITIMATE PRODUCT???
With any flash media purchased on Amazon (USB flash drives, SD cards, Solid State Drives, etc.), be VERY weary because there are TONS of fake products, many of which come from Amazon through their Fulfilled-by-Amazon program. Upon receiving the drive, you should manually verify that the drive is indeed what is advertised. You can use a free program like H2TestW, which tests drives by first writing X amount of data to the drive, and then verifying that X amount of data still remains after the drive is filled (with X being the advertised size of the flash drive or SD card.) If the card is a fake, when H2TestW attempts to read that 256gb of data written, but only gets back 4gb, it will alert you that your flash drive or memory card is a scam product. These fraudulent Sellers have no way of tricking this process. Additionally, perform several checks on the health of the media (using OS X's Disk Utility or Windows' DiskCheck), and if this is a solid state drive (or a hard disk drive for that matter), manually review the S.M.A.R.T. data (with a free program like Crystal DiskInfo) because it will show you whether or not the product you purchased is actually new because it logs usage statistics.

IF THE DRIVE HAS GOOD REVIEWS, DOES THAT MEAN IT IS A LEGIT PRODUCT???
Finally, while Amazon User Reviews can be of great benefit, there appears to be cause for concern here as well. It appears that many Sellers of these fraudulent flash drives and SD cards send boatloads of these fake products out to ranked Amazon Reviewers, and in many cases will get a positive review even if the product they sent is total garbage. It also appears that some Sellers go as far to create Amazon User Accounts and then publish a positive review on their own junk product to give it a higher rating than it deserves. So while Amazon reviews are certainly beneficial, there are limitations and this particular type of product seems very prone to abuse.

So, FWIW, if you are going to purchase this type of product on Amazon, regardless of who the Seller is, you should take several of the above steps to verify that the product you spent your hard-earned money on is indeed what was promised to you in the item's listing. YMMV.

This supplement is an adaptogen. It comes in gel caps with dark powder in them. The smell is reminiscent of a bulk herb and spice shop.

I found that when taking this once a day, I have had a much more calm, and orderly pattern of thought, I could handle the stress a bit more than without it, and it did help me to stop freaking out while I kept forgetting everything.

I had no bad side effects as a result of taking these pills. No digestive upset, no headaches, etc.
